title: Head of Security
description:
Tremendous is the global platform built for businesses to send payoutsâgift cards and moneyâto anyone, anywhere, instantly. We're trusted by 20,000+ organizations, from startups to giants like Atlassian, MIT, and United Way, to reach millions of recipients worldwide.

We're profitable and growing without outside investors. We're fully remote, with a high-documentation, low-meeting culture that leaves more time for the work that mattersâand for your life outside it. Our employee NPS sits in the high 80s.

We move billions of dollars through our systems. That makes security existential, and it's why we're making our first dedicated security hire.

About The Role

You'll be our first Head of Security. There's already a real foundation hereâbug bounty, pen tests, automated code and configuration scanning on the production and code side, phishing simulations on the people side. Youâll add to it across access and identity, SecOps and monitoring, incident response, vendor security, employee security practices, and policy. You'll own the whole posture.

This is a player-coach role. Early on, you'll do the scoping and the hands-on work yourself; this is not a role where you direct from above. As the work demands it, we're fully prepared to build a team hereâand we're looking to you to define what that team should be and when.

You'll report to the VP of Engineering, Tremendous' most senior technical leader. We've deliberately placed security with Engineering so you're set up to drive real implementation fastâembedded with the people whose work you're securing, not siloed in a compliance function. As the security function matures, we'll revisit this.

What You'll Do

  • Own Tremendous' security posture end-to-end, partnering with our engineering team on production infrastructure and code security.
  • Assess where we have gaps, prioritize them, and tackle our highest-leverage gaps first. Weâll have opinions, but you own the prioritization and implementation.
  • Treat incident response as core, not afterthought. We may not be able to prevent a breach, but your job is making sure it's small, contained, and that we know exactly what to do.
  • Drive security as a cultural shift across the companyâintroducing controls incrementally, working with teams rather than over them. "Yes, and," not "no."
  • Lead our AI-security posture. We invest heavily in AI tooling; your job is to manage that risk and enable it, not to ban it.
  • Define when and how to staff up the security function, and hire your own team.

What You'll Bring

  • Real, hands-on security experience at a company that scaledâideally as an early security hire who grew with the business through high growth.
  • Deep experience in at least one core security domainâproduct/production security, security operations, or access/identity and policyâwith enough range to reason across the others. You defined the security posture, not just executed someone elseâs playbook.
  • An engineer's mindset. You reach for code to solve problems and can read our codebase and understand our infrastructure (Ruby on Rails; TypeScript + React; PostgreSQL; Google Cloud). You won't write much day-to-day, but you're not lost in the code.
  • Judgment over checklists. You can explain the actual risk of a given decision, hold a firm line where it matters, and give ground where "best practice" doesn't apply to us or real business need pulls the other way. You can hold your own in a debate about whether to open up broad data access for AI tooling.
  • Bedside manner. You drive hard change by bringing the team around to your point of view, rather than just telling them no. Engineers and the rest of the company want to work with you.
  • Experience building or co-building a small security team is a plus.
  • Fintech, payments, or regulated-industry experience is a plus.

What's Cool About The Role

  • You define the function. First security leader, with the budget for the required tools and team.
  • A real mandate. The push for this hire comes straight from the founders.
  • We invest in your tools. Everyone has a $5k/month budget for AI tools. Use it.
  • Competitive pay and equity. Base salary $250,000â$330,000, plus meaningful equity.
  • Fully remote. Work from anywhere in the Americas.
  • Great culture. Read more about how we work in our public handbook.

Compensation Range: $250K - $330K

title: Data Analyst Assistant
description:
About the role
 The Data Analyst Assistant role is central to our current engagement with a Dubai-based investment firm that requires precise data handling and clear visualization. This position provides the quantitative groundwork that allows our principals to form a view on complex corporate governance and strategy questions. We need an assistant who can organize messy data sets into logical structures that reveal the health and performance of a holding company.

About Arabian Private Holdings
 Arabian Private Holdings was founded on the principle that many critical business problems do not fit the traditional large-firm consulting model. A board facing a succession question or a family group weighing a capital injection does not need a team of twelve associates and a hundred-page methodology deck. They need experienced partners who can sit with a problem, form a rigorous view, and defend it. We take on a limited number of mandates to ensure that every client receives direct attention from the principals who are actually accountable for the outcome. Our work covers corporate strategy, governance, and operating model efficiency for some of the most significant family groups, listed corporations, and government entities in the region. We focus on clarity over complexity. We operate as a remote firm, choosing to prioritize the quality of our analysis and the strength of our relationships over traditional office overhead or aggressive growth targets.

What you will do
  • Collect and organize financial and operational data from various portfolio companies for a Dubai-based investment.
  • Clean and validate data sets to ensure accuracy before they are used in client presentations.
  • Build simple, effective spreadsheets that track performance indicators for large holding companies.
  • Assist in drafting reports that translate numbers into clear written arguments for our principals.
  • Monitor industry trends and perform basic market research to support ongoing strategic mandates.
  • Maintain internal records to ensure that historical client data is easily accessible and correctly categorized.
  • Prepare charts and graphs that simplify complex financial structures for board-level reviews.
  • Support the audit of corporate governance documents by cross-referencing quantitative findings with qualitative reports.


What we are looking for
  • A clear understanding of basic statistics and a logical approach to problem-solving.
  • Proficiency in spreadsheet software with an ability to manage large amounts of information without errors.
  • Strong written skills and the ability to explain what a set of numbers means in plain English.
  • Curiosity about how large corporations and family groups operate in different sectors.
  • Precision in your work, where you check your own calculations before submitting them for review.
  • A degree or ongoing studies in a quantitative field such as economics, finance, or mathematics.


How we work
 We operate as a fully remote firm, which means we rely on clear documentation and asynchronous communication. Because our work involves sensitive mandates for high-profile clients, we maintain a high standard of professional conduct and data security. You will work closely with a principal who provides direct mentorship and expects you to form your own view on the data you analyze. We do not value long hours for the sake of appearances. Instead, we focus on the rigor of the output and the clarity of the logic. This remote model allows us to hire individuals based on their intellectual capability rather than their physical location, ensuring we can provide the best possible advice to our clients.

What the role offers
  • A paid entry-level position with a competitive compensation package for the current market.
  • Direct exposure to high-level corporate strategy and governance mandates.
  • Mentorship from experienced principals who have managed some of the largest holding companies in the region.
  • The flexibility of a permanent, full-time role that is entirely remote.
  • Practical experience in forming a rigorous view on business performance and portfolio health.

title: Data Entry Administrator
description:
About PulseMediaNL

PulseMediaNL is a forward-thinking digital media company committed to delivering high-quality content, innovative marketing solutions, and exceptional customer experiences. We value accuracy, efficiency, collaboration, and continuous improvement. As our team grows, we are seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented Data Entry Administrator to support our daily operations by maintaining accurate and reliable data across multiple platforms.

Position Overview

The Data Entry Administrator is responsible for accurately entering, updating, verifying, and maintaining company data while ensuring the highest standards of quality and confidentiality. This role requires excellent attention to detail, strong organizational skills, and the ability to work independently in a remote environment. The successful candidate will help ensure that business records remain complete, accurate, and accessible, contributing directly to operational efficiency.

Key Responsibilities

  • Identify and correct errors, inconsistencies, or duplicate entries.
  • Organize and maintain digital files, records, and documentation.
  • Perform routine data quality checks and audits.
  • Generate reports and summaries as requested by management.
  • Assist with importing and exporting data between various software platforms.
  • Maintain confidential information in accordance with company policies and applicable privacy regulations.
  • Collaborate with internal departments to obtain missing or updated information.
  • Prioritize tasks to meet deadlines while maintaining a high level of accuracy.
  • Support administrative projects and perform additional data-related tasks as assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent; an associate's or bachelor's degree is an advantage.
  • Previous experience in data entry, administrative support, or office administration preferred.
  • Excellent typing skills with a high level of accuracy.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing error-free work.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel and Word.
  • Experience using Google Workspace, including Google Sheets and Google Docs.

  • Strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Reliable internet connection and a suitable remote work environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with CRM or ERP software.
  • Familiarity with database management systems.

  • Experience working remotely in a professional environment.

Key Skills

  • Data entry accuracy
  • Time management
  • Organization
  • Attention to detail
  • Communication
  • Problem-solving
  • Computer literacy
  • Multitasking
  • Confidentiality
  • Team collaboration

What We Offer

  • Fully remote work environment.
  • Competitive salary.
  • Flexible working schedule where applicable.
  • Paid time off and company holidays.
  • Opportunities for professional development and career growth.
  • Supportive and collaborative team culture.
  • Ongoing training and skill development.
  • Performance recognition and advancement opportunities.
  • Access to modern digital collaboration tools.

Success in This Role

The ideal candidate consistently delivers accurate work, meets deadlines, maintains confidentiality, communicates effectively with colleagues, and demonstrates a proactive approach to improving data quality and administrative processes.

Equal Opportunity Employer

PulseMediaNL is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all employees are treated with respect and provided equal opportunities.

If you are a detail-oriented professional who enjoys working with data and thrives in a remote environment, we encourage you to apply and become part of the PulseMediaNL team.

Success Measures

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, and related medical conditions), gender, gender identity or gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin or ancestry, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, medical condition (including cancer and genetic characteristics), age (40 and over), marital status, military or veteran status, genetic information, or status as a victim of domestic violence, assault, or stalking. title: Senior SAP functional in-house Consultant (m/f/d)
description:
At Flix, we offer a dynamic work environment with competitive pay, strong growth opportunities, and a tech-driven approach to making travel more accessible, sustainable, and affordable.  

We're looking for an experienced SAP functional Consultant (m/f/d) to join our ERP Finance team at Flix, in Berlin or Munich. 

In the Foundation Division of FlixTech, the ERP Finance team is responsible for the platform that powers our financial backbone: accounting, controlling, procurement, period close, and the integrations that connect them to the rest of Flix. We're setting up a new ERP system for our Train business (FlixTrain) with a first focus on Finance and Procurement. 

As our in-house SAP expert, you'll work closely with our Finance and Procurement teams as well as external partners to make sure the new ERP fits our needs: today and in the long run. After go-live, you'll be the person who owns, evolves and continuously improves the SAP solution from the inside. 

This role is well suited for someone who enjoys ownership, working close to real business problems, and combining solid SAP craftsmanship with a long-term, in-house perspective 

About the Role

  • Act as Flix's in-house SAP expert during the implementation of our new ERP, with a focus on Finance and Procurement. 
  • Translate business requirements from Finance, Procurement and adjacent functions into clean, scalable SAP solutions. 
  • Work closely with external implementation partners during design, build, testing and cut over. 
  • Support data migration, test management, and go-live preparation from a Flix-side ownership perspective. 
  • Take long-term ownership of the SAP solution after go-live: enhancements, change requests, integrations and continuous process improvement. 
  • Contribute to building broader SAP capability within the ERP Finance team thought teaching and mentoring. 
  • Be a trusted advisor to Finance and Procurement stakeholders on what SAP can do for 

About You

  • 7+ years of experience as an SAP Consultant (incl. 5+ years in S/4HANA), with a strong focus on Finance (FI/CO) and Procurement (MM). 
  • Additional working knowledge in SAP Supply Chain and Asset Management modules. 
  • At least two full end-to-end SAP implementations, ideally in a company of similar size and complexity to Flix. 
  • Solid understanding of core finance and procurement processes: General Ledger, Accounts Payable / Receivable, Fixed Assets, Controlling, Purchase-to-Pay. 
  • Experience working with external system integrators and the confidence to engage with them as an equal partner. 
  • Comfortable engaging with senior Finance and Procurement stakeholders and translating between business and SAP language. 
  • Structured, pragmatic, delivery-oriented; strong communication and facilitation skills. 
  • Based in Germany, you're fluent in German and English. 

We recognize that everyone carries a unique set of valuable skills and experiences. If you think you could have an impact even though you don't meet 100% of the requirements, we still encourage you to apply. We want to hear from you!  

What We Offer

  • Travel perks: 12 free Flix vouchers + 12 discount vouchers for friends & family. 
  • Work from (M)Anywhere: Depending on your role, work from another location for up to 60 days per year. 
  • Hybrid work model: We are an office-first company, but we offer flexibility to balance work and life. 
  • Wellbeing support: Access confidential 1:1 counselling, courses, and stress management for yourself and up to four family members. 
  • Learning & Development: Take advantage of language classes, training courses, and expert-led sessions to grow your skills. 
  • Mentoring Program: Connect with experienced colleagues to gain insights and accelerate your career. 

To view more local benefits specific to each office location, please check out this link: Locations - Flix Career

Why Join Flix?

At Flix, you'll find teams that rally together to overcome challenges and spark creativity. We believe in ownership culture - giving you the freedom to take initiative, make an impact, and shape your own career path.
As we continue to expand across the globe, you can make a real difference in how we work.

If you're ready to grow and lead your journey, Flix is the place for you!

title: Senior Data Scientist, Workforce Management Analytics
description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

About the Support Group

As the name Support Group implies, this group is responsible for the core part of the customer experience journey that has got Wolt top-notch ratings in app stores. 

During the years we've invested a lot in the in-house built support tooling as we believe that it's the only way we can ensure the satisfaction of all of our customers and partners in each of the 25 countries that we operate in. We take huge pride in our customer operations' quality, so on top of building delightful support experiences in our consumer app we also want to proactively identify and solve issues even before our customers and partners even notice something might be wrong.

About the Support Analytics Team

Our Support Analytics team's main goal is to deliver an amazing Customer, Merchants & Courier support experience while optimizing our operations by providing actionable insights and quantifying the impact of those actions on the overall business. 💡 

You'll be part of this team working with top Data Science and Analytics Engineering professionals.

What you'll be doing

As a Senior Data Scientist at Wolt, your role involves diving into our data to solve crucial business problems. The scope of this role ranges from diagnosing problem areas to identifying solutions to designing experiments and ultimately influencing decision-making. This is a rare, operational, and actionable data-driven experience. When you join this team, you will be driving action from the frontlines, rather than just doing yet another analytics role.

Your job will mainly focus on driving operational efficiency with the Workforce Management (WFM) team and optimizing resource allocation by creating accurate scheduling and intraday forecasts, simplifying forecasting processes, building and supporting KPI dashboards, conducting root cause analysis for SLA improvements, exploring cost optimization opportunities, managing the capacity plan framework, enhancing the WFM data pipeline, and uncovering data-driven insights to refine planning, scheduling, reporting, and intraday management.

Our humble expectations

Required:

  • 5+ years of experience in a data science or analytics position
  • Experience building forecasting models and time series analysis (Prophet, SARIMA, Holt-Winters or similar)
  • Experience in Cost Analysis and What-if Scenario Analysis
  • Deep knowledge of statistical packages in Python or R
  • Proficiency in writing structured and efficient SQL queries for large data sets
  • Ability to influence and advise senior stakeholders Good to have:
  • Experience using ML for forecasting
  • Experience working with ML engineers/ML platform
  • Building data pipelines using Airflow or similar tools

What we offer

  • The online delivery platform that Wolt is building will offer you interesting and complex challenges, together with the opportunities to create a big impact with your skills. Lots of geolocational and temporal data in real-time, combined with differences in the economics and dynamics of the cities we operate in, make Wolt both a challenging and interesting company to practice analytics.
  • You have the chance to decide the ways of working: a hybrid, at the office, or remote in Berlin. 💙 
  • You would get to work in a company culture where we take ownership beyond the obvious, do common things uncommonly well, we think big but stay humble, do right by people, we treat others kindly and justly, recognize that if we don't learn, we won't stay still but fall behind and keep in mind that Luke was Yoda's greatest achievement.

Next steps

The position will be filled as soon as we find the right person, so make sure to apply as soon as you realize you really, really want to join us!

For any further questions about the position, you can turn to Senior Talent Acquisition Partner - Zhanna Filintseva via  

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

description:

In this role, you sit inside the Founders' Office and work on the decisions that set SPREAD's direction. Your Mission

  • Own the strategy cycle from analysis through to a written strategy the leadership team commits to, then translate it into company OKRs, goals, and the quarterly review rhythm that keeps every team measured against them.

  • Run the operating rhythm of the leadership team across the weekly leadership meeting, monthly workshops, and half-year offsites. Set the agenda, prepare the discussions and decisions, and track every decision and task.

  • Build and steer SPREAD's partner ecosystem across hyperscalers, systems integrators, strategy consultancies, and tech companies, and convert those relationships into commercial opportunities, co-marketing and integrated offerings.
  • Manage SPREAD's portfolio of senior industry advisors, former executives from the automotive and defense industry, to generate commercial opportunities and capture deep industry insights and expertise.
  • Step into selected high-stakes commercial opportunities and ongoing engagements alongside Sales, Product, Value Realization, and Engineering, bringing structure and pace.

Your Experience

  • 4+ years in strategy consulting, investment banking, or an operating strategy role inside a scale-up, with end-to-end ownership of your own workstreams and direct exposure to the client side.

  • AI-native working style. You use AI tools daily to scale your output across research, analysis, drafting, and workflow automation. SPREAD is an AI-first company, and every team member operates accordingly.
  • Based in Berlin or close enough for regular in-office collaboration.

Why SPREAD?

  • Work on the questions that decide where a company building engineering intelligence for the products that move the world goes next, with the founders and the leadership team as your direct counterparts.
  • Own initiatives end to end with full visibility across Product, Engineering, Sales, Finance, and the partner ecosystem, and see your work land in the company's direction and in decisions that actually get made.

title: Growth Intelligence & AI Analyst
employer: Lovebetter Gesellschaft für männliche Sexualität mbH
description:
Jobbeschreibung

Warum gibt es diese Rolle - und warum jetzt?

Lovebetter wächst in eine neue Phase. Wir haben starke Inhalte, eine klare Mission, Gavin als Gesicht der Marke und eine gewachsene Marketingdatenbank, deren Potenzial wir künftig deutlich systematischer nutzen wollen. Gleichzeitig wollen wir Marketing nicht länger nach Bauchgefühl steuern, sondern klar verstehen, welche Themen, Kanäle, Funnels und Kontaktpunkte wirklich Wachstum erzeugen.

Dafür suchen wir dich.

Als Growth Intelligence & AI Analyst bist du die Person, die aus Daten, KI, CRM, Content-Performance und Marketinglogik ein klares Steuerungssystem baut. Du erkennst Muster, entwickelst Hypothesen, prüfst Tests und hilfst uns, schneller bessere Entscheidungen zu treffen.

Diese Rolle ist bewusst breiter als ein klassischer Analystenjob. Du sollst nicht nur Dashboards bauen, sondern aktiv mitdenken, wie Lovebetter mehr qualifizierte Leads, bessere Funnel, stärkere Lifecycle-Kommunikation und planbareren Umsatz aufbaut.

Wofür Lovebetter steht

Wir lösen sexuelle Probleme wie vorzeitigen Samenerguss oder Erektionsprobleme mit Männern und befähigen sie, ihre innere Stärke, sexuelle Zufriedenheit und Lebensqualität von innen heraus zu transformieren.
Unsere Arbeit wirkt weit über den Einzelnen hinaus: auf Partnerschaften, Familien und kommende Generationen.

Wir suchen jemanden, der Verantwortung übernimmt, Wirkung messbar macht und weiß, dass echter Impact aus Exzellenz, Struktur und Umsetzungskraft entsteht.

Deine Mission als Growth Intelligence & AI Analyst

Du machst Lovebetter messbarer, lernfähiger und wachstumsstärker. Du verbindest Business Intelligence, CRM, KI, Content-Performance und operative Growth-Tests. Du analysierst, welche Themen Männer wirklich bewegen, welche Inhalte Vertrauen aufbauen, welche Funnels funktionieren und welche Kontaktsegmente aktiviert werden können.

Dabei arbeitest du eng mit dem CMO, Content Production, Chatter, Agenturen und später CRM-/Lifecycle-Strukturen zusammen. Gerade am Anfang wirst du auch Themen mit abdecken, die noch nicht sauber verteilt sind: CRM-Analyse, Reaktivierungslogik, kleine Website- oder Landingpage-Tests und operative Growth-Experimente.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Reporting & Business Intelligence aufbauen: Du entwickelst ein schlankes KPI- und Reporting-System für Content, Funnel, CRM, Paid, SEO, Chatter und Sales-Schnittstellen. Ziel ist, jede Woche klar zu sehen, was funktioniert, was nicht funktioniert und wo Wachstum entsteht
  • Hypothesen entwickeln und testen: Du formulierst klare Growth-Hypothesen, zum Beispiel zu Hooks, Zielgruppen, Freebies, Landingpages, CRM-Segmenten oder Funnel-Schritten, und prüfst diese anhand von Daten
  • CRM-Potenziale sichtbar machen: Du analysierst bestehende Marketingkontakte, entwickelst Segmentierungslogiken, identifizierst Reaktivierungshebel und misst, welche Lifecycle- oder Upsell-Impulse funktionieren
  • AI für Analyse, Research und Marketingsteuerung nutzen: Du setzt KI ein, um schneller Muster zu erkennen, Content- und Funnel-Daten auszuwerten, Zielgruppenfragen zu clustern, Tests vorzubereiten und Entscheidungsgrundlagen zu schaffen
  • Operative Growth-Tests mitdenken und umsetzen: Du bleibst nicht nur im Analysemodus. Du denkst kleinere Tests auf Landingpages, Website, Formularen, E-Mail-Strecken oder Funnel-Schritten mit und kannst einfache Anpassungen operativ begleiten

Was diese Rolle besonders macht

  • Direkter Wachstumshebel: Deine Analysen beeinflussen, welche Themen, Kanäle, Funnels und CRM-Strecken wir priorisieren
  • Daten statt Bauchgefühl: Du baust die Grundlage dafür, dass Marketingentscheidungen messbar, vergleichbar und lernfähig werden
  • KI als echter Produktivitätshebel: Du nutzt AI nicht als Spielerei, sondern für Research, Mustererkennung, Hypothesen, Reporting und bessere Entscheidungen
  • Breite Verantwortung: Du arbeitest nicht nur im Dashboard, sondern denkst CRM, Content, Funnel, Website-Tests und operative Growth-Experimente mit
  • Gestaltungsraum: Du hilfst dabei, Lovebetter von einem content-getriebenen Marketing-Team zu einem klaren Revenue-Marketing-System weiterzuentwickeln

Dein Impact

Wenn du deinen Job exzellent machst, entsteht:

  • ein Marketing-System, das klar erkennt, welche Maßnahmen wirklich Wachstum erzeugen
  • bessere Entscheidungen bei Content, CRM, Paid, SEO, Chatter und Funnel
  • aktivierte Bestandskontakte statt ungenutzter Datenbank
  • mehr qualifizierte Leads durch saubere Hypothesen und Tests
  • ein Weekly Growth Reporting, das dem Team Orientierung und Priorität gibt
  • ein skalierbares Zusammenspiel aus KI, Daten, CRM und Customer Journey

Klingt nach dir?

Dann freuen wir uns, dich kennenzulernen.

Schick uns keine Standardbewerbung.
Erzähl uns lieber:

  • welche Marketing-, BI- oder Growth-Systeme du bereits aufgebaut oder verbessert hast
  • wie du KI heute konkret in deiner Arbeit nutzt
  • welche Hypothesen oder Tests du schon entwickelt und ausgewertet hast
  • wo du schon Verantwortung für Reporting, CRM, Funnel oder Performance getragen hast
  • und warum du glaubst, dass genau du Lovebetter datenbasiert und wachstumsseitig auf das nächste Level bringst

Stellenanforderungen

Wen wir suchen (und wen nicht)

Diese Rolle passt zu dir, wenn …

  • du mindestens 3 Jahre Erfahrung in Marketing Analytics, BI, Growth, Performance Marketing oder Revenue Operations hast
  • du exzellent mit Zahlen, Daten und Zusammenhängen arbeitest und daraus klare Wachstumshebel ableitest
  • du KI täglich nutzt, um Analysen, Research, Hypothesen, Segmentierungen oder Prozesse schneller und besser zu machen
  • du CRM, Funnel und Lifecycle-Marketing verstehst und erkennst, wie aus Kontakten qualifizierte Leads und Umsatz entstehen
  • du Hypothesen klar formulieren, testen und auswerten kannst
  • du strukturiert, eigenständig und lösungsorientiert arbeitest und dem CMO klar sagen kannst: „Das ist der Hebel. Das sollten wir testen. Das sollten wir stoppen.“

Diese Rolle ist nichts für dich, wenn …

  • du Zahlen nur „berichtest“, aber daraus keine klaren Entscheidungen ableitest
  • du KI spannend findest, sie aber nicht aktiv in deinen Arbeitsalltag integrierst
  • du dich ausschließlich als Dashboard- oder Reporting-Person verstehst
  • du kein Interesse daran hast, CRM, Content, Paid, Website und Funnel zusammenzudenken
  • du dich in Analysen verlierst, ohne ins Handeln zu kommen

Deine Aufgaben:

  • Betreuung und Weiterentwicklung unserer (SaaS-)Anwendungen im Unternehmen
  • Einrichtung, Installation und Konfiguration von Standard-Software
  • Dokumentation und Konzeption digitaler Geschäftsprozesse
  • Planung und Einführung neuer Software- und IT-Lösungen
  • Entwicklung von Schnittstellen zur Verbindung von Standardlösungen
  • Automatisierung wiederkehrender Aufgaben mit Tools wie Make, Zapier oder durch API-Integrationen
  • Fehleranalyse, Störungsbeseitigung und kontinuierliche Prozessoptimierung

Tools & Technologien im Fokus:

  • Make & Zapier: Diese Low-Code-Plattformen ermöglichen dir, komplexe Workflows zu automatisieren, Systeme miteinander zu verbinden und datengetriebene Prozesse effizient umzusetzen. Du entwickelst automatisierte Abläufe zur Optimierung interner Geschäftsprozesse und sorgst für eine reibungslose Datenintegration zwischen verschiedenen Anwendungen.

title: Principal of backend
description:
About SchemeServe

SchemeServe is insurance software like no other.

Hosted in the cloud for MGAs, brokers and insurers, the SchemeServe platform boasts unique flexibility, unstoppable innovation and truly Obsessive Support.

Started in 2000 by our CEO, Adam, SchemeServe has grown from strength to strength, never having taken outside investment. We're proud of how far we've come and how loyal we've stayed to our Core Values.

We're fully remote (we were doing it before it was fashionable!), although we get together twice a year for Team Retreats.

We prize self-development and encourage everyone to keep learning and challenging themselves. Free books? Mentoring? Professional development? You got it.

We also offer flexible working, paid charity days, a fantastic, relaxed and open company culture and free biscuits through the post.

We genuinely believe this is the best place you could ever work.

If you're excited, good! So are we.

Come and join the Insurtech revolution!

Principal Backend Engineer

UK Remote

We're looking for an exceptional Principal Backend Engineer to help make backend engineering across SchemeServe better.

You'll be one of the most technically experienced engineers in the organisation and the CTO's primary technical partner for backend engineering, helping shape our architecture, engineering principles and technical direction.

But this isn't primarily a feature delivery role and your job isn't to personally build everything you help design.

Your real job is to make our engineering organisation better at building great software.

You'll work alongside engineers and teams, helping solve difficult problems, challenging their thinking and developing their technical skills and judgement.

What We Mean By Principal

This is a deeply technical role.

You'll need the depth to understand complex backend systems, architecture, security, performance, resilience and maintainability; review designs and implementations; spot risks; and challenge experienced engineers.

But technical knowledge alone isn't enough.

We want someone who understands there isn't always one "correct" way to build software.

Patterns, standards and best practices are useful tools. They aren't commandments.

We care about finding the most appropriate solution to the problem in front of us.

That means understanding the problem, business, existing platform, risks and likely future – and making pragmatic decisions based on the trade-offs.

Sometimes the right answer will be a new service or technology.

Sometimes it'll be improving what we already have.

Sometimes the boring solution really is the best solution.

We're quite comfortable with that.

How You'll Lead

Success in this role comes through influence rather than authority.

We don't want every difficult technical decision to end with:

"We'd better ask the Principal Engineer."

If an engineer proposes an approach you disagree with, we don't just want you to replace it with your own.

Understand their thinking. Ask questions. Challenge assumptions. Explore the trade-offs. Share your experience.

And be prepared to change your own mind too.

The goal is to leave that engineer better equipped to solve the next problem, not just holding the answer to this one.

Your technical impact should multiply through the people around you.

You'll remain close enough to the code to understand what's actually happening and occasionally roll up your sleeves to prototype, investigate a difficult problem or unblock a team.

But if after a year you've personally written loads of brilliant software while everyone around you is working exactly as they were before, we haven't succeeded.

The Technical Challenge

Our platform has been evolving for more than 25 years.

At its heart is a mature C# .NET Framework 4.7 monolith, alongside an expanding ecosystem of modern C# .NET 10 and TypeScript services.

Our backend estate includes:

  • .NET Framework and modern C#/.NET.
  • TypeScript services.
  • Microsoft SQL Server, PostgreSQL and Redis.
  • Azure cloud infrastructure.
  • Cloudflare platform services.
  • API-first architecture.
  • Git-based development workflows.

We're continuing to modernise, but we're not interested in modernisation for modernisation's sake.

We aren't trying to win an award for having the most fashionable architecture diagram.

We want a secure, reliable and maintainable platform that can support SchemeServe for many years to come – and we want you to help us decide what should evolve and, just as importantly, what doesn't need changing.

What You'll Do

You'll work closely with our CTO and engineering teams to:

  • Shape our backend engineering strategy, architecture and technical direction.
  • Help engineers make better technical and architectural decisions.
  • Develop sensible engineering principles and guardrails without replacing good judgement with rules.
  • Guide the continued evolution of our monolith and modern service-based platform.
  • Coach and mentor engineers, developing their technical skills and judgement.
  • Review significant designs and architectural decisions and challenge unnecessary complexity.
  • Champion security, quality, testing, observability, resilience and performance.
  • Identify technical risks and help teams navigate them.
  • Evaluate technologies and patterns based on their value to SchemeServe rather than their popularity elsewhere.
  • Balance long-term engineering quality with short-term business needs.
  • Occasionally contribute directly to implementation when that's genuinely the best way to help.
  • Be a generally awesome person.

What We're Looking For

You'll need:

  • Deep expertise in modern backend engineering and strong commercial C#/.NET experience.
  • Strong knowledge of software architecture, distributed systems and API design.
  • Experience with mature legacy applications and modern service-oriented architectures.
  • Strong cloud architecture experience, ideally Azure.
  • Excellent understanding of databases, security, testing, maintainability and modern software delivery.
  • Experience shaping engineering principles and practices across teams.
  • A track record of making engineers around you better through mentoring, coaching and technical leadership.
  • The ability to challenge experienced engineers constructively without becoming a gatekeeper.
  • Strong opinions, loosely held – the confidence to challenge and the humility to change your mind.
  • Excellent communication and the ability to influence without relying on authority.
  • Excellent technical judgement, balancing quality, complexity, risk, cost and business value.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who asks:

"What's the right solution for us?"

rather than:

"What's the way everyone else is doing it?"

Nice To Have

  • Experience modernising large monolithic applications.
  • Commercial TypeScript backend experience.
  • Cloudflare or edge technology experience.
  • SaaS platforms at scale.
  • Financial services, insurance or another regulated industry.
  • Observability, platform engineering or SRE experience.
  • AI-assisted development and engineering productivity tooling.

You don't need to tick every box.

If you've got the technical depth, judgement and ability to make engineers around you better, we'd rather have a conversation than lose a great candidate because you haven't used one particular technology.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first year:

  • Engineers are making stronger technical and architectural decisions with greater confidence.
  • Our engineering principles are understood rather than blindly followed.
  • Technical discussions are constructive, pragmatic and result in clear decisions.
  • Security, reliability, maintainability and performance concerns are identified earlier.
  • We've made sensible progress modernising our platform without adding complexity for complexity's sake.
  • You've made a lasting positive impact on both our software and the people who build it.

Ultimately, we don't want SchemeServe to become dependent on you for every difficult technical decision.

We want SchemeServe to become better at making those decisions because you're here.

Why Join SchemeServe?

  • Fully remote UK-based role.
  • Twice-yearly company retreats.
  • Flexible working.
  • Dedicated professional development support.
  • Paid charity days.

Friendly, supportiv...

What is Optimisation in Flex?
The Optimisation chapter is the mathematical and algorithmic engine of the KrakenFlex platform. While other chapters manage physical asset connectivity or ingest market signals, this domain is responsible for the intelligence that decides exactly what every asset should do, second by second, to maximise both grid stability and financial returns.

The teams within this chapter build and maintain the real-time dispatch engines, predictive forecasting models, and algorithmic solvers that handle massive multi-asset portfolios. This involves translating complex market rules, physical asset constraints (like battery degradation curves, state-of-charge limits, and ramp rates), and fluctuating price signals into optimised execution strategies.

The defining challenge for this chapter is scaling computational performance alongside our rapid asset growth. Running complex, multi-variable mathematical models in tight real-time windows requires immense efficiency. The core tension lies in balancing the demand from data science and quantitative engineering to introduce increasingly sophisticated models with the strict platform requirement for absolute reliability, low latency, and cost-effective cloud compute.

Ultimately, this chapter must move away from bespoke optimisation routines tailored to individual markets or asset types. Your goal is to architect a highly performant, modular optimisation core that uses standard abstract layers, allowing us to roll out new algorithms or expand into new global territories without rewriting the underlying engine.

🚀 What you’ll own:
The Flex platform is built on autonomous Chapters, which are collections of specialists focused on delivering a core service or business outcome, defined by the unchanging nature of the energy business (independent of technology, hardware, or regional differences). A Head of Engineering leading a Chapter is a senior leadership role combining strong product thinking, engineering judgement, operational awareness, and people leadership. They manage managers and senior individual contributors, helping teams own their product surfaces, make sound trade-offs, and deliver reliably.

This role requires influencing beyond its formal remit, spotting cross-team patterns, clarifying ownership and decision-making, and driving initiatives to turn recurring issues into visible actions with owners, dates, and measures of success. title: Head of Compliance Product
description:
We're hiring a Head of Compliance Product to lead the products at the heart of Elliptic and define what they become in the age of AI.

Compliance is where Elliptic began and where our commercial core sits today. Some of the world's largest exchanges, banks and government agencies rely on our screening, monitoring and investigation products, and the industry they serve is at an inflection point. Compliance teams everywhere are looking to AI to make their work dramatically more efficient, freeing their people to focus on the judgement calls that genuinely need a human, with every automated decision auditable and explainable. Elliptic is building that future with our customers, not just for them, and this role owns it.

You will lead the product managers responsible for our core compliance portfolio, spanning wallet and transaction screening, continuous monitoring, on-chain investigations and risk configuration, and you will drive the product side of our agentic compliance programme alongside our design partners. Much of what you build will have no precedent. You will be inventing the category, inside the company with the data, intelligence and customer trust to win it.

This is a player-coach role reporting to the VP of Product. You will lead and grow a team of product managers and personally own some of the hardest problems on the roadmap. The product organisation is centred in London with a growing US presence.

 
 

What you'll do

  • Own the vision, strategy and roadmap for Elliptic's compliance portfolio, and define what these products become as AI reshapes how compliance work gets done.

  • Lead product for our agentic compliance programme: AI capabilities that make compliance work faster and better, with auditability and explainability designed in from the start.

  • Lead, coach and grow a team of product managers. Hire well, develop people deliberately, and set the standard for how a modern, AI-augmented PM works. Developing product talent is a core output of this role, not a side effect.

  • Stay obsessively close to customers, in creative ways: Methods such as design partnerships, analyst shadowing, product instrumentation, and internal dogfooding before anything ships come naturally to you to increase the chances of success. Convert ambiguous market signal into a clear view of what to build and why.

  • Prioritise ruthlessly. Demand will always exceed capacity. Sequence zero-to-one bets against the needs of products customers depend on today, and say yes or no credibly, with reasoning people can engage with.

  • Execute with rigour, raising velocity and quality together. Own outcomes, not shipping dates. Use AI across your own workflow and your team's to learn faster and ship better at the same time, in a domain where mistakes carry real consequences.

 
 

What this role is not

  • Not a compliance officer role. You are building the products compliance teams use, not running a compliance programme.

  • Not a caretaker role. The core products are successful and deeply embedded; the mandate is reinvention.

  • Not a management-only layer. You will lead product managers and personally do product work on the hardest problems.

 
 

Who we're looking for

  • 10+ years building software products, including leading and developing product managers, with people who are better because they worked with you.

  • A genuine zero-to-one track record: an ambiguous problem in a complex domain, taken from nothing to a product real users depend on.

  • Depth in financial crime compliance from the product side (transaction monitoring, screening, KYC/EDD or investigations), built inside an exchange, a bank, a fintech or a compliance technology company.

  • Working knowledge of crypto and blockchain as a baseline; deep blockchain analytics experience is a strong plus.

  • AI-native: AI is embedded in how you work and build every day, you have shipped AI or agentic capabilities to production, and you raise the AI capability of teams around you. If AI has not materially changed how you build product in the last two years, this is not the right role.

  • Deep executional rigour: you break complex problems into shippable steps, sweat the details that determine quality, and reliably carry work over the line.

  • High self-sufficiency: you find high-value opportunities no one assigned you, create clarity rather than wait for it, and are comfortable owning a broad remit while the map is still being drawn.

  • Continuous systems thinking: you look for the repeatable system behind every one-off fix, building leverage so each problem solved makes the whole team permanently faster.

  • A data-informed operating style: you instrument what you ship, argue from evidence, and change your mind when the data disagrees.

  • Judgement under ambiguity: you know which decisions to make fast and which to hold open when precedent does not exist.

  • Comfort in regulated, high-stakes environments: you treat trust, explainability and defensibility as features, and operate well at the tension point between innovation and regulatory reality.

  • Restlessness about velocity and quality: you treat "that's just how long it takes" as a claim to be tested.

If you're energised by ownership, invention, and building side by side with customers in a high-stakes domain, we'd love to hear from you.

As our Risk & Controls Operations Associate, you will serve as the first line of regulatory and operational control for Investa’s platform. Working together with our Head of Risk & Compliance and Co-Founders, you will help own the day-to-day execution of our key operational controls spanning CASS oversight, onboarding operations, financial crime monitoring, and execution control.

This is a critical, high-visibility role within a fast-scaling financial trading environment. You will bridge regulatory oversight with practical execution: verifying client money flows, resolving dealing and onboarding exceptions, and ensuring our operations adhere strictly to FCA standards as our operating model expands from sub-account clearing into in-house custody.

  • Management Information: Own and gather key performance indicators covering all aspects of the business for committee reporting and oversight.

  • Financial Promotions: Review and approve marketing campaigns, product copy, and social media promotions to ensure strict alignment with FCA Financial Promotion and Consumer Duty rules.

  • Regulatory Change: Assist in implementation of regulatory change in the UK or elsewhere to ensure compliance with new rules that apply to the Firm.

  • Third Party Risk Management: Point of contact for vendors and outsourcing partners to oversee and coordinate information sharing for incident closure & customer support.

  • Trade surveillance: Provide first line review of alerts generated through trade surveillance for signs of market abuse. Oversee the closure of alerts and applicable audit trail.

You can choose whether you want to pave a path as a high-level individual contributor or step into management as we scale - you shape your career.

description:

Revenue operations and Salesforce

  • Maintain and improve the revenue operations framework across GTM, including pipeline governance, forecasting cadence, sales process discipline and commercial reporting.

  • Your team acts as the business owner for Salesforce and connected revenue systems, ensuring they support current, often high stakes, operating needs, data quality and consistent adoption.

  • Support on integration and usage of other relevant systems and how they form the process, such as Planhat and Clari.

  • Define, monitor and interpret key commercial metrics such as bookings, recurring revenue, conversion rates, deal cycle, retention, productivity and forecast accuracy. Drive data consistency in both usage and interpretation across teams as it relates to measuring commercial health.

  • Support change management by communicating the context, purpose and value of work clearly, engaging stakeholders and embedding new ways of working.

ISO9001 and quality management

  • Own the ongoing maintenance of ISO9001 accreditation and ensure the quality management system remains effective, current and audit-ready.

  • Coordinate internal audits, external assessments, corrective actions and continuous improvement activity.

  • Work with process owners to ensure quality standards are embedded into day-to-day business operations.

  • Track non-conformities, risks and improvement actions through to completion.

People leadership and team development

  • Define and align team goals with the Operations direction, setting clear expectations and holding the team accountable for delivery.

  • Manage workload, priorities, performance and an allocated team budget where applicable, balancing multiple high-priority deadlines and responding calmly to unexpected risks or issues.

  • Build capability within the team through regular feedback, mentorship, development planning and knowledge sharing, with limited people growth decisions made with supervisory approval.

  • Strong Salesforce ownership or administration experience, with the ability to translate business needs into practical system and process requirements.

  • Confident with PowerBI reporting and data visualisation capability, with strong analytical skills and attention to detail.

  • Commercial awareness and confidence working with revenue, pipeline, forecasting and performance data.

  • Experience defining and leading medium-to-large cross-functional projects or initiatives, managing senior stakeholders independently and navigating ambiguity with sound judgement.

  • Understanding of ISO9001, quality management systems, audit preparation and continuous improvement principles.

  • People management experience, including coaching, prioritisation, performance management and team development.

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex data or process issues clearly to different audiences.

We have one mission. To help businesses grow. To make data easier. And to make the world a better place. We’re not a start-up. Not anymore. But we’ve not been around that long either. What we are is a collection of bright, passionate minds harnessing complexities and helping our clients and their communities. One culture, made of many. Heading in one direction – the future.

We want you to feel welcome, valued, and respected - because it’s your individuality and passion that make you Q. We see that, and we celebrate it. That’s why we’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
TL;DR – We’re looking for an exceptional Forward Deployed Engineer to help build the future of AI-powered software creation. You will be a founding member of our FDE function, working directly with our customers to translate ambitious ideas into real products. This is a hands-on software engineering role: you will design, write, and ship production code. It’s a unique opportunity to scale a new discipline from scratch and solve problems with AI that no one has solved before.

 

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

 

About the role

Most engineering roles place you either close to the product or close to the customer. This role gives you both.

You’ll build alongside customers at the frontier of what Lovable can do, solving technically difficult problems across our frontend, backend and AI systems. The goal isn’t simply to make individual deployments successful: it’s to identify what should become part of the Lovable platform and then build it.

As one of our first Forward Deployed Engineers, you’ll also help define the function - from its engineering standards and ways of working to how it collaborates with customers and our core product teams.

If you want to stay deeply hands-on while shaping a product, a team and a new engineering discipline, this is that role. As you’ll be working directly with customers, travel up to 50% could be required depending on needs.

 

What we’re looking for

  • 8+ years of hands-on experience building and shipping production software

  • Strong full-stack engineering fundamentals, including React and TypeScript on the frontend and robust backend development

  • A track record of writing maintainable, well-tested code and owning what you build in production

  • Strong architectural thinking and familiarity with distributed systems

  • Ability to prototype rapidly and turn successful experiments into production-quality solutions

  • Exceptional product intuition and ability to work directly with users

  • Comfort operating with high ambiguity, agency, and end-to-end ownership

Bonus if you’ve:

  • Worked on agentic AI systems or built with LLMs before

  • Led zero-to-one product development

  • Worked in a founding or early startup environment

 

What you’ll do

  • Work directly with customers to understand their workflows, needs, and problems

  • Turn ambiguous requirements into clear technical designs and working production systems

  • Design, code, test, deploy, and operate solutions across Lovable’s frontend and backend

  • Translate insights from real usage into foundational platform improvements

  • Own projects end-to-end—from discovery and architecture through shipping and iteration

  • Debug complex issues across application, infrastructure, and AI-system boundaries

  • Shape how Forward Deployed Engineering operates at Lovable, including its engineering standards, rituals, and playbooks

  • Contribute to core product strategy, technical decisions, and cultural foundations

 

Our Tech Stack

  • Backend: Golang & Rust

  • Frontend: React, Typescript

  • Cloud: Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, multiple LLM providers

  • Tooling: Github Actions, OTEL, Grafana, Terraform, and more

 

How we hire

  1. Fill out a short form and hop on a brief intro call with our recruiting team.

  2. Complete a quick live coding exercise.

  3. Show us how you approach problems during several technical interviews.

  4. Show us something you’ve built that makes you proud.

title: Staff Software Engineer - Enterprise Platform
description:
TL;DR

We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer to help define the future of Lovable Enterprise.

Some of the world's largest companies are already building with Lovable. Now we're building the platform that allows them to deploy Lovable securely, reliably, and on their own terms.

How do you let an enterprise customer deploy Lovable inside their own cloud without slowing product development? How do you build a platform that works seamlessly across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud without compromising security or developer experience? Those are the kinds of problems you'll solve.

You'll define the technical direction for the platform that powers Lovable Enterprise—from cloud architecture and sandboxing to networking, encryption, and identity.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

Why join now?

Very few engineering roles offer this level of ownership. You'll help define a platform rather than inherit one. Many of the hardest architectural decisions haven't been made yet, giving you the opportunity to shape the foundation of Lovable Enterprise alongside engineering leadership.

Whether you've been a Staff Engineer, Principal Engineer, founding engineer, or CTO, we're looking for someone who's already operated with this level of ownership—and wants to do it again on an even bigger stage.

What you'll do

You'll define the technical direction for the platform that lets enterprise customers run Lovable securely and at scale.

You'll spend your time writing software, making architecture decisions, mentoring engineers, and working directly with customers on problems that don't have established playbooks. Examples include:

  • Defining the architecture for enterprise deployments across AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, including deployments into customer-controlled environments.

  • Building cloud-agnostic systems that give customers flexibility in how and where they run Lovable.

  • Designing secure sandboxing and runtime environments for running untrusted code at scale.

  • Setting the technical bar for networking, encryption, identity and enterprise infrastructure.

  • Building the internal platform that helps our engineering teams ship faster.

  • Mentoring engineers and raising the engineering bar across the organisation.

  • Working directly with enterprise customers and cloud providers on complex infrastructure challenges.

What we're looking for

We're looking for a Staff-level (or equivalent) Software Engineer with deep platform and infrastructure experience who have set technical direction before. This is a role for engineers who enjoy building software that powers infrastructure, if you’re from a traditional DevOps background this is less likely to be a good fit.

This is the role for you if you have:

  • Strong programming skills in Go or Rust, or a comparable systems language (C++, Java or similar)

  • Experience building enterprise products and working with enterprise customers.

  • Designed and scaled distributed systems in production that are used by multiple teams.

  • Built on Kubernetes (or a similar orchestrator) as a platform, not just deployed to it.

  • Hands-on experience designing and running production systems across more than one major cloud (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud), with deep expertise in at least one.

  • A product mindset. You care about the people using the systems you build, not just the systems themselves.

  • Experience operating at Staff, Principal, founding engineer, or CTO-level scope.

And deep experience in some of these:

  • Shipping software into customer-controlled environments (BYOC, VPC, self-hosted, air-gapped).

  • Sandboxing and isolation (containers, microVMs, multi-tenant security).

  • Enterprise identity, networking and encryption (SSO/SCIM, KMS/BYOK, private networking).

Our tech stack

  • Languages: Go, Rust, TypeScript

  • Cloud: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Cloudflare

  • Infrastructure: Kubernetes, Terraform, Temporal, OpenTelemetry, CI/CD

  • Data: PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Firestore, Spanner, BigQuery

 

About your application

Please submit your application in English—it's our company language.

We encourage anyone excited by the role to apply, even if your current title isn't "Staff Software Engineer." What matters most is the scope you've owned and the impact you've had.

title: Senior Sales Director
description:
Life at Plume

At Plume, we believe that technology isn't about moving faster, it's about making life's moments better. Which is why we've built the world's first, and only, open and hardware-independent service delivery platform for smart homes, small businesses, enterprises, and beyond. Our SaaS platform uses WiFi, advanced AI, and machine learning to create the future of connected spaces—and human experiences—at massive scale.

We now deliver services to over 60 million locations globally and have managed over 3 billion devices on our platform. We're expanding rapidly, pioneering a new category, and we achieved our Series F funding in just four years. Our customers include many of the world's largest Internet Service Providers (ISPs) who look to Plume to help them evolve their smart home offerings while gleaning insights from their own data. 

With a bias for action and a love for being trailblazers, the team at Plume embodies a combination of relentless curiosity and imaginative innovation. We challenge ourselves to think in ways that other companies don't, work to do what should be done (rather than what can), and if we can't do it exceptionally well, we don't do it. It's how we've assembled a team of world-class builders, thinkers, and doers. And it's how we're reinventing what's possible every day.

Role Description:
Plume works with Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to run the connected experience inside their
subscribers' homes and small businesses. Our platform sits between their network and the people using
it, managing WiFi performance, security, device visibility, care and the digital services layered on top. We
are used at scale by some of the largest ISPs across North America, Europe, Asia and the Middle East.
The UK and Ireland are mature and concentrated markets. The number of ISPs that matter is small, they
are well known to us, and most already have an established approach to managing the connected home.
Success here depends on building credibility at a senior level, shaping how these organisations think
about the experience they deliver to their subscribers, and then proving that value at scale.
We are looking for someone who is at their best in a small number of large, complex accounts rather
than in a broad prospecting territory.
It is a role with real ownership. You will be the face of Plume in the region, working directly with our
executive team and with senior leaders at some of the best-known ISPs in the market.

Responsibilities:
• A named list of UK and Ireland ISPs, covering both new logos and the growth of existing
deployments into new services, subscriber tiers and lines of business.
• A multi-million-dollar annual quota carried across new business and installed base expansion.
• The full cycle: executive access, discovery, business case, technical validation and POC,
commercial modelling, procurement, contract, and a clean handover into delivery. You stay
accountable through launch.
• The relationship map inside each account. Not a single champion, but the CTO, the Chief Product
or Consumer officer, the owner of customer care and operations, and whoever holds the broadband
P&L.
• A virtual team pulled from solutions engineering, product, delivery, finance, legal and executive
sponsorship. You direct it. You do not wait for it.
• Accurate forecasting. Deals of this size move, and we would rather know early than late.
• A clear read on the market: how ISPs in the region are approaching the connected home, where
their priorities are shifting, and what that means for our roadmap. You are our eyes in the territory.

Qualifications:
This role calls for someone who already understands how ISPs buy. Their decision cycles, stakeholder
structures and commercial models are specific to the industry, and the experience we are looking for
reflects that.
• A track record selling hardware, software, cloud or platform solutions directly to ISPs, with evidence
of recurring or subscription-based commercial models. Your experience should be with ISPs as the
buyer, rather than with a telco's enterprise IT function as one account among many.
• Ownership of deals in the multi-million-dollar ACV range, with 9 to 24 month cycles, formal
procurement, and an established solution already in place.
• Fluency in ISP economics. ARPU and attach rates, churn and retention drivers, cost to serve,
contact volumes and handling time, truck roll avoidance, CPE fleet lifecycle and ODM relationships,
NPS. You should be able to build a credible business case yourself before a solutions engineer is in
the room.
• Experience winning business where the customer already had a solution in place, whether bought
or built in-house. That is a different commercial conversation, and we place real weight on it.

• Existing senior relationships across UK and Ireland ISPs, or a specific and realistic plan for building
them inside two quarters.
• MEDDPICC applied in practice rather than in theory. Expect to walk us through a live deal from your
current role against it.
• Comfort operating without a finished playbook. Our product moves, our commercial models evolve,
and parts of this territory are still being defined. You will be building as you sell.
• Consistent quota attainment, and the ability to explain honestly where you missed and why.
• Willingness to travel regularly across UK and Ireland, and occasionally across EMEA.

About Plume

As the creator of the only open, hardware-independent, cloud-controlled experience platform for ISPs and their subscribers, Plume partners with over 400 ISP customers, including some of the world's largest such as Charter, Liberty Global, and J:COM. 

Using OpenSync, the most widely supported open-source, silicon-to-cloud framework for smart spaces, Plume's software-defined network allows ISPs to decouple their service offerings from hardware and rapidly curate and deliver new services over a multi-vendor, open-platform architecture.

description:

Create compelling campaigns, brands and experiences for causes that matter.   • Lead and inspire: Working closely with your colleagues, you'll develop a vision for our client's creative success. You'll guide the development and implementation of campaigns, appeals and creative platforms, from initial presentations through final delivery.

  • Pre-tax season ticket loans
  • Cycle to work (up to £2000)
  • Remote work flexibility

We approach in-office working with a hybrid model, with presence in our office required at two days per week.

The team

You'll be a senior member of the London team bringing in new clients and, as a leader, defining and improving the work we're creating. You will also be a part of our global creative director team who meet regularly for creative inspiration.

Some things we're looking for

  1. 6+ years in senior creative role, ideally with hands-on designing experience. At least some of this experience working on fundraising and mobilisation campaigns.
  2. Experience in leading and collaborating with teams of designers, copywriters, strategists and creatives - taking insight that has been shaped and developing compelling, digitally-driven ideas and products.
  3. Strategy-led: able to clearly articulate design or strategy related dilemmas, and offer multiple solutions with a clear link back to the strategy and insights. 
  4. Comfort and passion for creative testing, co-creation with clients and audiences, and constructively consolidating feedback from global stakeholders to improve the work. 
  5. Impeccable presentation skills: able to explain the reasons behind a particular design or creative strategy, and guide clients through difficult decision points. Experience in pitching a strong advantage.
  6. Deep knowledge of persuasion strategies & tools: copywriting, social influence, brand advocacy, fundraising, UX and experience design.

  8. An area of expertise or passion in the design world (be it fundraising, design, UX, communications or social change) that you can harness and upskill wider team members with as a thought leader within the wider company.
  9. Industry-leading quality of work: you produce inspiring work that stands out, is flawless in execution, and innovative in thought. You are both a doer and a thinker, and your work reflects that.

title: Senior Technical Programme Manager - Money
description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

About the Team

At DoorDash we're building the industry's most scalable and reliable delivery network to support our three-sided marketplace of consumers, merchants, and dashers. TPMs on our Engineering teams provide fundamental support to the underlying technology services as well as the engineers building these services. It's no simple task, but it wouldn't be interesting if it was!

About the Role

Money is DoorDash's organisation responsible for the financial products and infrastructure that enable transactions across DoorDash, Wolt and Deliveroo. The domain owns how consumers pay, how merchants and couriers are paid, and how money is recorded, reconciled and reported, covering payment processing, payment methods, payouts, invoicing, financial ledgers and regulatory compliance.

We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to help scale Money Domain. You will lead important engineering wide initiatives across Invoicing Platform, Payment Instruments, amongst others; working with Engineering, Product, Operations, and business leaders to deliver dependable, scalable Money capabilities for the business. Programs will span backend services, partner and merchant integrations, and regulatory / compliance products. They require strong technical judgment, cross organisational coordination, stakeholder management, and ownership of results.

You will report into the centralised global Technical Program Management team in Engineering, through a manager based in London. This is a hybrid role based in our London office in Cannon Street.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Drive Money Domain's Most Strategic Programs - You will partner closely with Engineering and Product leadership, Strategy & Operations, and cross-functional teams to turn Money Domain's strategy into executable technical programs. 
  • Lead Complex Cross-Organization Execution — Money Domain interacts with capabilities across consumer, merchant, courier, order and enterprise domains, payment processing, payouts, fraud and risk, regulatory compliance, accounting, financial data and platform infrastructure. You will establish clear ownership and milestones, surface critical dependencies and tradeoffs, and drive alignment across teams when the path forward is not obvious.
  • Bring Technical Depth and Systems Thinking - You will develop a deep understanding of the architecture, integrations, data flows, and operational systems behind Money Domain (Financial Systems). You will engage in technical designs, identify scaling and reliability risks, understand how decisions in one part of the system affect end-to-end consumer, rider/ courier, and merchant experiences, and help teams make pragmatic tradeoffs.
  • Turn Ambiguity into Strategy and Action - Many of our hardest problems do not begin with a clean scope or a single owner. You will truth-seek across technical and business inputs, frame the problem, clarify the definition of success, develop a point of view on risks and options, and create an execution path that teams and leaders can align behind.
  • Connect Engineering Execution to Business Outcomes - You will understand the merchant, partner, customer, and economic outcomes behind the work and use that context to guide prioritization and execution. Whether the goal is expanding access to DoorDash logistics, improving delivery quality and reliability, enabling new partner use cases, or improving cost to serve, you will help teams stay focused on the technical work that matters most to the business.

We're excited about you because…

  • You're experienced in working with engineering teams on  large-scale distributed systems and/or b2b products. You can speak to system architecture, scalability and reliability decisions, and design trade offs.
  • You're a strong leader with the ability to collaborate and build relationships across organizations, bridge gaps between teams, and successfully influence without authority.
  • You have strong ownership, urgency, and drive. You are willing to roll up your sleeves and dive into the details to understand and drive your programs.
  • You have excellent written & verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate with confidence, clarity, and focus. You can convey concepts and considerations to non-experts and experts alike.
  • You've engaged with Engineering teams on product & platform development with a thorough understanding of software development processes and project planning.
  • You are pragmatic and detailed in your approach and focus on progress, not perfection.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree with experience in Computer Science, Software Engineering or other related discipline.
  • 5+ years recent experience as a Technical Programme Manager at a technology/ FinTech company, in Financial Systems.
  • Experience with regulatory compliance in Financial Systems, e.g. SOX, PSD2, or equivalent would be an advantage.
  • Experience in large-scale distributed systems and system architecture.
  • Experience working directly with engineering teams on product development, with a thorough understanding of software development processes, system architecture, and scalability trade-offs.
  • Project planning and execution skills that include reviewing technical design documents, estimating, and scheduling.

description:

Street Group is a fast-moving B2B SaaS business, grown in Manchester but on a UK-wide mission to make moving house as easy as buying a car. We're PE-backed and scaling fast with an ambitious growth plan, and we're looking for an FP&A Analyst to help us get there.


As we grow, our revenue streams are becoming more varied by the month. That means more reporting, more complexity, and a finance function that needs to proactively help drive growth.


This is an opportunity to help expand our FP&A function, you won't be slotting into a fixed process. You'll be shaping it while owning the data and supporting the models that feed our board packs and investor reporting.
